title: Prove repeatable generated field and mesh determinism
description: Repeated editor regenerations of the same apparent creature state have produced materially different triangle/vertex counts. Establish whether the divergence begins in SDF sampling, active-cell classification, contour extraction, or upstream resolved-input state. Use exact field and mesh fingerprints, repeated runs, and the complex culling fixture before changing the algorithm. A valid result must produce identical field and extraction fingerprints for identical resolved input and generation settings. If field fingerprints differ, inspect background-generation input isolation and SDF/Burst behavior; if fields match but meshes differ, inspect active-cell/contour extraction; if both match but Unity presentation differs, inspect mesh binding/presentation lifecycle. Do not solve observed variance with smoothing or arbitrary tolerances.

comments.author: ChatGPT
comments.body: 2026-09-11 evidence: fresh generated meshes showed detached polygon islands and successive regeneration logs varied from roughly 10.6k to 12.1k vertices / 21.3k to 24.1k triangles. The branch now contains GenerationIntegrityTests plus exact field/mesh fingerprints to identify the first divergent stage. Unity execution is the closure gate.
